description:
ICEBOUND is an interactive Arctic simulation platform that uses NASA-ISRO NISAR satellite data to investigate permafrost degradation before irreversible damage occurs.

The platform allows users to explore hidden ground-ice conditions, distinguish seasonal movement from persistent thaw-related changes, and test preventive interventions.

Its flagship TwoEarth Experiment demonstrates how two landscapes with nearly identical satellite observations can conceal dramatically different futures.
summary: ICEBOUND turns real NASA/ISRO NISAR L-band browse at Eight Mile Lake into a clear drill decision. The app walks from “same look from space” to underground soil photos, a Sept/Nov Track 116 browse wipe from ASF DAAC, a labeled soil twin, and a ranked short-core plan. It shows why satellites alone can miss buried ice, and keeps claims honest: browse change, not calibrated γ⁰. Built for Space Apps 2026 “Dancing with the SARs” by Gitanjali Penumatsa (NUS) and Aniket Mimani (NTU).
details: ICEBOUND is a five-step web app: Start → Two undergrounds → NISAR → Soil twin → Drill plan. Users compare mineral soil vs ice-wedge field photos, wipe September vs November NISAR GCOV browse on Track 116 Frame 056 (ASF DAAC), run a labeled 1D soil twin to see settlement diverge with buried ice, then rank where one short core helps and export a plan. Stack: Vite, React, TypeScript, Three.js. Creative fit: connects real NISAR browse change to an actionable ground decision while labeling browse limits and the twin as a what-if scenario, not a survey.
dataRefs: NASA/ISRO NISAR L-2 GCOV browse (ASF DAAC)
